text:
Warm, salt-tinged winds rush towards the lone isle, a bastion of life after countless miles of ceaseless waves. White wings widely spread to rise along 
with it as the seabird glides over weaves of coral. Spirals of color, teeming with crustaceans fight over every inch of exposed coral reaching past the water, 
creating great strands of calcified land that sparkles in the high noon sun. For a while the bird glides over this bustling seascape, feeling it unsafe to land 
as even the corals themselves writhe to catch prey. She soon spots true land as the relentless waves break against stone cliffs. A vinnirex pup, its maw 
covered in blood from the slain scavick its kin recently caught, looks up at the white winged bird, and turns its head to follow her flight across the rising 
hills of woodlands to the north. 
With a steady beat of wings she scales high over the dense canopy, a deeply uncomfortable feeling of danger felt when she looks down at the undulating 
green mass of leaves. Suddenly, sunlight glints off a stream of liquid that fires off from below, arcing thankfully too low. Her fear, a combination of 
instinct and deep seeded nature are justified as a green scaled ynnil glowers from the canopy it clings to; its potential meal now long out of range. For 
miles the seabird flies over thick forest. In the distance to the east, a loud crash of trees can be heard, one of tearing branches and falling trunks, causing 
small quakes disturbing birds and insects in their thousands, the seabird sees this and keeps her distance. For the white winged bird has an ancient 
pathway to follow, one she has never navigated herself but feels its direction ingrained in her genetic memory.
Exhaustion leeches the seabird's strength with every beat of her wings as she soars higher. Grass and dirt transition to slate gray stone beneath her, 
snow drifts thicken as she rises higher still over rushing herds of thick shelled insects. Though it chills her white feathers, the west bound winds push 
her onward, until at last, sailing over outcrops untouched by the tread of beasts for eons, the last snow covered peak breaks and she sees her ancestral 
destination.
Passing the last peak with a release of absolute exhilaration, she flows downward with the land, feeling the wind whip past her outstretched feathers, 
quickly descending into rolling hills and silver rivers. Finally, the seabird sees the distant island she had sought all this time, the place of her birth and 
the one she defied so many odds to return to lies before her. Nestled in the bay, like a sanctuary, rests an outcropping of stone rings steeply rising from the 
waters, entirely covered in hundreds of her kin. Their cries are a cacophony of warmth and welcome, an instinctual bloom of warmth that other creatures 
may call happiness. The brilliant blue crests from an array of males, beckon her to the nests they prepared for her and other potential mates, as the white 
winged bird makes her final descent. The exhausted seabird’s eyes spot a nest with just the right amount of smooth stones and a male with as vibrant and 
strong crest as she could ever ask for. With a final beat of her wings, she settles into the finely crafted nest and clacks her beak, feeling fulfilled.
Seasons upon the Shores
Rising from the temperate oceans north of the equator, the island of Sol’Kesh has been isolated from the main continents for eons, 
their landmasses far distant and unseen. Any creature born on these shores may think this is the world in its entirety and, besides 
long distance migratory animals, it is. These creatures, far removed from their continental origins, have drastically changed through 
isolation and island gigantism, creating a unique ecosystem that finds each living species competing for every niche to call their own 
and propagate.
The climate is often comfortably mild, warm currents bloom with life across its teeming shores. While the summer months can get 
blistering hot, particularly on the dry wastes of the western Grayfynn plains. The east on the other hand, commonly enjoys steady 
rainfall that enriches the fertile soil, though this causes many swamplands to fester along the north and south. Fall sees an incredible 
change of color throughout the woods that blanket the west, and up in the mountain steppes, Last Bloom’s coniferous trees retain their 
green needles throughout the chill of winter. The cold months that follow soon slow down the arthropod megafauna and forces many 
herbivores to migrate away from the higher altitude lands into the warmer fields and prairies nearer the lowland shores. Though there 
are days of snowfall, it rarely lasts long enough to settle on the ground beyond the deep coverage seen on the central mountain range of 
the Splitspine mountain and Tundrus highlands, where the draffers hunt in droves. By spring, it is rare not to find a day without rain 
in the west, the gloom of the sky ushering in an absolute bloom of fungi that dominate the landscape with a dank vibrancy that creates 
a foundation for all life to grow from.
